rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **new Cartesian sign convention** measures all distances from the pole, against incident light as negative, and gives f < 0 for concave, f > 0 for convex mirrors (NEB 2021, 3m). For paraxial rays a mirror of radius R focuses at $f = R/2$ (NEB 2024, 4m), and similar-triangle geometry yields the **mirror formula** $\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$ (NEB 2024, 5m). Magnification is $m = h'/h = -v/u$.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Sign errors kill mirror-formula marks:** in the Cartesian convention u is negative for a real object and f is negative for concave mirrors.  ·  **Negative magnification = inverted (real) image**, not a "negative-size" image.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Do not substitute the thin-lens equation for the mirror equation.  ·  f=R/2 assumes a spherical reflecting surface and small angles.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***NEB 2024*** — u = −10 cm, f = −15 cm → v = +30 cm, m = +3 (virtual, erect, magnified).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQs: sign convention 2021 3m; magnification + focal length 2022 3m; numerical 2022 4m; mirror formula derivation 2024 5m; f = R/2 2024 4m; numerical 2024 3m; magnification definition 2024 2m.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: A concave mirror has R=40 cm. Find signed f in the stated convention.  ·  Describe two principal rays for a concave-mirror construction.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): A concave mirror of f = 20 cm forms a real image twice the object size. Find u.** — m = −2 = −v/u → v = 2u. With u negative and v negative: 1/(2u) + 1/u = 1/f → 3/(2u) = 1/(−20) → u = −30 cm; object 30 cm in front, image 60 cm in front.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: State the sign convention explicitly before any derivation — the 2024 5m asks for it.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — One Equation for Every Mirror Image Real or virtual, magnified or diminished — every image a spherical mirror forms obeys a single compact relation: $\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$. NEB loves it: the 2024 paper carried both the 5-mark derivation and the 4-mark $f = R/2$ proof.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2021, 2022, 2024) ### 2.1 Sign convention (NEB 2021, 3m) **New Cartesian convention:** 1. All distances are measured from the **pole P** of the mirror. 2. Distances measured **in the direction of incident light** are positive; against it (in front of the mirror) are **negative**. 3.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 68:** the formula reproduces every qualitative case of image formation. - **To f = R/2:** the mirror formula's "1/f" is 2/R — aperture geometry in disguise. - **To refraction formula (Unit 15):** $\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$ for lenses is the refracting twin of the mirror formula.
